llm_reasoning.analyte_preparation_explanation: Vitamin C is treated as solid L-ascorbic acid and is directly dispensed into the KCl-containing experiment vial at a calculated mass of 26.419 mg. It is dissolved during the same 300 second stirring operation used for electrolyte preparation. Because ascorbic acid can oxidize during storage in aerated aqueous solution, prepare only immediately before use and transfer the vial to the electrochemical substation for prompt measurement after mixing and pre-test pH measurement.
assumptions: Vitamin C is supplied as solid L-ascorbic acid with molecular weight 176.124 g/mol and is available for loading into a Quantos cartridge at position 2. If Vitamin C is not physically available as a Quantos-compatible solid, the requested experiment cannot be executed without providing that reagent.
KCl is supplied as anhydrous potassium chloride with molecular weight 74.5513 g/mol and is available in Quantos cartridge position 1.
Water is available as a pump-compatible liquid on syringe-pump channel 1.
The selected 0.100 M KCl electrolyte is unbuffered because no additional buffer components or compatible liquid acid/base reagents were explicitly made available.

No nitrogen purge is included because nitrogen availability was not explicitly specified. Dissolved oxygen may contribute background current, so a fresh blank 0.100 M KCl measurement may be run separately if baseline subtraction is required.
The CV control program scans from the start potential to the specified vertex potential and reverses automatically for each of the exactly five complete cycles.

concentration_calculations.calculation_explanation: For 0.100 M KCl in 15.0 mL: required moles = 0.100 mol/L x 0.0150 L = 0.00150 mol. Required mass = 0.00150 mol x 74.5513 g/mol = 0.11182695 g = 111.82695 mg. The planned Quantos mass is rounded to 111.827 mg. Actual concentration = (0.111827 g / 74.5513 g/mol) / 0.0150 L = 0.10000004 M.

For 0.010 M L-ascorbic acid in 15.0 mL: required moles = 0.010 mol/L x 0.0150 L = 0.000150 mol. Required mass = 0.000150 mol x 176.124 g/mol = 0.0264186 g = 26.4186 mg. The planned Quantos mass is rounded to 26.419 mg. Actual concentration = (0.026419 g / 176.124 g/mol) / 0.0150 L = 0.01000015 M.

llm_reasoning.constraint_validation_summary: One experiment vial and one electrochemical slot are used. Two solid cartridges are required, which is within the maximum of eight. One liquid pump channel is used, which is within the maximum of four. Water volume is exactly 15.000 mL, satisfying the required electrode immersion volume and vial-volume limit. Each Quantos dispensing mass is below the 200 mg per-cartridge capacity: KCl is 111.827 mg and L-ascorbic acid is 26.419 mg. The experiment uses aqueous solvent, an Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) reference electrode, a 2 mm platinum working electrode, and a platinum wire counter electrode. The requested potential limits and exactly five cycles are explicitly defined.
llm_reasoning.drying_explanation: No analyte film is deposited; therefore, no drying step is applicable. The platinum working electrode is dried after washing and before immersion in the prepared solution.
llm_reasoning.electrode_deposition_explanation: No electrode deposition is performed because the requested mode requires Vitamin C dissolved in the electrolyte. The 2 mm platinum working electrode is polished, washed, dried, and then immersed directly in the prepared analyte/electrolyte solution.
llm_reasoning.electrolyte_preparation_explanation: Dispense 111.827 mg KCl from Quantos cartridge position 1 into one clean 20 mL experiment vial. Dispense 26.419 mg Vitamin C from Quantos cartridge position 2 into the same vial. Dispense 15.000 mL water through liquid-pump channel 1. Mix with a stirrer bar for 300 seconds to dissolve both solids homogeneously. Measure and record the solution pH immediately before CV. The 15.000 mL aqueous volume ensures electrode immersion and does not exceed the experiment-vial capacity.
llm_reasoning.parameter_selection_logic: Aqueous 0.100 M KCl provides adequate ionic conductivity while retaining the user-requested chloride supporting electrolyte. The potential program starts at -0.100 V and scans to the required +0.700 V versus Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl), covering the expected anodic oxidation region of ascorbic acid on platinum. A 100 mV/s scan rate is a practical initial characterization rate that limits prolonged exposure of the air-sensitive analyte while providing a resolved voltammetric response. A 5 mV potential increment provides adequate potential resolution. Exactly 5 cycles are specified as required. AUTO current ranging is selected because the oxidation current of 10 mM Vitamin C at a 2 mm Pt disk can vary with electrode condition, diffusion, solution pH, and catalytic surface behavior. The platinum working electrode is polished before the run to improve reproducibility. The solution is not nitrogen-purged because nitrogen availability is not explicitly provided; the sample should instead be prepared fresh and measured immediately after mixing. Measure and record pH immediately before and after CV using the electrochemical substation pH capability.
llm_reasoning.selected_mode_explanation: The required configuration is analyte_in_electrolyte because Vitamin C must be dissolved directly in the freshly prepared 0.100 M KCl supporting electrolyte and measured in the same experiment vial. No electrode deposition or drying step is used.

metadata.description: Cyclic voltammetry characterization of 0.010 M Vitamin C (assumed L-ascorbic acid) dissolved in freshly prepared 0.100 M KCl aqueous supporting electrolyte. The experiment uses a 2 mm diameter platinum working electrode, platinum wire counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) reference electrode.
metadata.user_prompt: Perform a cyclic voltammetry experiment to characterize 0.01 M Vitamin C as an analyte dissolved in the electrolyte. The Vitamin C should be prepared in the electrolyte and measured using the electrochemical substation. Prepare 15 mL of 0.1 M KCl supporting electrolyte using available solid KCl and water. Use the available platinum working electrode (d = 2 mm), platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) reference electrode. Select appropriate electrolyte composition, Vitamin C concentration, CV parameters, mixing/preparation steps, and safety precautions based on the capabilities and constraints provided in the system context, starting with a potential window of -0.1 to +0.7 V versus Ag/AgCl and exactly 5 cycles. The resulting experiment must be directly executable by the CVLab platform.

cross_contamination_risks: Vitamin C residues can adsorb or remain on the platinum working electrode; polish, wash, and dry the working electrode before the run and wash all electrodes afterward.
KCl and Vitamin C powder carryover can occur if Quantos dispensing heads or cartridge exteriors are contaminated; use dedicated cartridge positions and clean external powder residues.
Do not cross-contaminate the Ag/AgCl reference electrode filling solution with the sample or polishing slurry.
handling_precautions: Wear laboratory coat, safety glasses, and suitable disposable gloves when loading cartridges, handling electrodes, and removing the experiment vial.
Load L-ascorbic acid and KCl as dry powders into separate Quantos cartridges; avoid inhalation and clean powder spills using approved laboratory procedures.
Prepare the Vitamin C solution immediately before measurement, protect it from unnecessary light exposure, and begin CV promptly after mixing because ascorbic acid oxidizes in air over time.
Polish the platinum working electrode before measurement, then wash and dry it to remove polishing residue before immersion in the sample.
Rinse the working and counter electrodes between experiments with water to minimize carryover. Do not rinse or polish the reference-electrode junction.
Confirm all three electrodes are immersed in the 15 mL solution and electrically connected before starting the potentiostat.
hazards: L-ascorbic acid powder may cause minor eye, skin, or respiratory irritation; avoid generating dust during cartridge loading.
Potassium chloride is a low-hazard salt but powder contact and dust inhalation should be avoided.
The prepared Vitamin C solution is mildly acidic and may irritate eyes or damaged skin.
Electrical and pinch hazards are present during potentiostat operation, electrode polishing, and robotic vial handling.
The Ag/AgCl reference electrode contains concentrated KCl filling solution and may introduce trace silver-containing contamination into waste.
waste_disposal: Collect the post-CV aqueous KCl/Vitamin C electrolyte and all electrode-rinse liquids in an appropriately labeled aqueous electrochemical waste container.
Do not discharge waste to the drain because reference-electrode leakage can introduce trace silver-containing material.
Dispose of used gloves, wipes, and polishing residues according to local laboratory solid-waste procedures.
